# `unawaited-async`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: correctness · Profile: none · Default: warning · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports an `std.Io` future, group, or select whose tasks are never awaited or
cancelled, or that an early exit no `defer` covers can leave pending.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

A task started with `io.async`, `io.concurrent`, `Group.async` or
`Select.async` holds resources until it is awaited or cancelled, and it usually
points into the frame that started it. A `Future` that is dropped, or a group
or select that goes out of scope with tasks still pending, leaks those
resources, and an `async` task may never run at all; a task that runs after
its frame is gone reads and writes freed stack memory.

## When it fires

The rule reports a local `Future` that is never awaited or cancelled, a future
discarded with `_ =`, and a local `Io.Group` or `Io.Select` that spawns tasks
but is never awaited or cancelled (`awaitMany` and `cancelDiscard` also finish
a select). Returning the owner, storing it, or passing it to another function
transfers the obligation.

It also reports the first `try` or `return` that can leave the function after a
task starts and before the first `await` or `cancel`, unless a `defer` or
`errdefer` registered before that exit finishes the task, as in
`defer group.cancel(io);`. For tasks spawned in a loop, exits anywhere in the
loop count, since earlier iterations' tasks are still pending. Exits inside
test blocks are not reported, because a failed `try` already fails the test.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const std = @import("std");

fn work() void {}

fn start(io: std.Io) void {
    var pending = io.async(work, .{});
    _ = &pending;
}
```
